stem.evolab.island_hint_meadow: Mild weather and abundant food. Look for variation before changing anything.
stem.evolab.island_hint_snow: Pale coats blend into snow. More insulation helps in the cold.
stem.evolab.island_hint_drought: Food is scarce. Heavy insulation and long legs both carry energy costs.
stem.evolab.island_hint_forest: Dark coats are harder to spot. Longer legs improve escape but cost energy.
stem.evolab.island_scene: Living Island habitat. Use the organism selector below to inspect any creature.
stem.evolab.island_loading: Growing your island… You can already use every simulation control.
stem.evolab.island_fallback: Habitat map · 3D is unavailable on this device. All experiments and family records still work.
stem.evolab.island_variation_ring_legend: Blue outer rings mark the chosen trait range. All organisms remain on the island.
stem.evolab.island_trial_camera_hint: Drag to orbit · compare the population data below
stem.evolab.island_specimen_view_hint: Specimen view · isolated on a display stand for inspection. Drag to turn the view; the organism’s place on the island stays unchanged.
stem.evolab.island_camera_hint: Drag to orbit · tap a creature to meet it · pale rings mark your selection, gold rings its family
stem.evolab.island_intro_follow_title: A life is short. A family can keep going.
stem.evolab.island_intro_advance_title: Who will leave the next generation?
stem.evolab.island_intro_result_title: You have a family story to investigate.
stem.evolab.island_intro_meet_body: Meet a spriglet on this volcanic island. Its coat, insulation and legs come from the genes it was born with.
stem.evolab.island_intro_follow_body: Follow this spriglet to mark its descendants with gold rings. Both parents contribute genes to every offspring.
stem.evolab.island_intro_advance_body: Advance once to sample survival and inheritance. Your spriglet might leave offspring, or its lineage might end. Both are discoveries.
stem.evolab.island_intro_result_body: Open the family journey to see who inherited this ancestry. Revisit any recorded generation to meet its relatives.
stem.evolab.island_family_machine_kicker: Follow the family, not a fixed trait
stem.evolab.island_family_machine_intro: Travel through recorded generations. The island follows your cursor; no new survival or inheritance is rolled.
stem.evolab.island_family_chart_alt: Family trait mean and full range compared with the whole population. Values use a 0–100 scale. Exact data are in the complete family record.
stem.evolab.island_family_climate_lines: Vertical dotted lines mark recorded habitat changes, not proof of their effects.
stem.evolab.island_family_missing_trait: No family members live in this generation, so its mean and range are undefined. The family curve ends at its last recorded members; it does not fall to zero.
stem.evolab.island_family_ancestor_singl: This first point is one actual ancestor. Move forward to see variation among its descendants.
stem.evolab.island_family_mean_change: Family mean change since the ancestor
stem.evolab.island_family_change_help: These are different individuals, not an ancestor changing during its lifetime.
stem.evolab.island_family_everyone: Every resident here shares this ancestor. The family and whole-population curves now describe the same organisms.
stem.evolab.island_family_range_help: The shaded band spans the lowest to highest actual family values. It is not a confidence interval. Higher values are not automatically better; descendants also inherit from their other parent.
stem.evolab.island_journey_before: This spriglet has not been born in the generation you are viewing. Visit its first generation to start the story.
stem.evolab.island_journey_start: This is the spriglet you started following. Later generations show its descendants, counted once even when both parents belong to the family.
stem.evolab.island_journey_continues: These are new individuals with a shared ancestor. They also inherit from their other parent; sharing ancestry does not mean keeping the ancestor’s exact traits.
stem.evolab.island_journey_ended: No descendants of this spriglet remain here. Other families still live on the island. A lineage can end through chance, survival differences, or leaving no offspring.
stem.evolab.island_journey_extinct: The whole population has ended, including this family. Revisit the last breeding round to see what happened.
stem.evolab.island_journey_count_help: Family members · share of this generation
stem.evolab.island_journey_ancestor_died: The ancestor did not survive this round.
stem.evolab.island_journey_ancestor_no_o: The ancestor survived, but left no offspring in this round.
stem.evolab.island_journey_survival: family members survived the next recorded breeding round
stem.evolab.island_journey_relative: Meet a descendant in this generation
stem.evolab.island_journey_trait_table_h: Trait values use a 0–100 scale. A dash means no members exist for that measure or the next survival round is not recorded. Family members are counted once, even through two related parents.
stem.evolab.island_detective_intro: Compare two real spriglets. Use their traits to predict who has the better chance, then discover who actually survives and leaves offspring.
stem.evolab.island_detective_unavailable: Use a present generation with at least two residents and a survival round left.
stem.evolab.island_detective_clues: Look at all three traits: camouflage, warmth and escape can help, but insulation and long legs also carry energy costs. Trait values below are on a 0–100 scale.
stem.evolab.island_detective_neutral_clu: Trait selection is off. Food and random chance still affect survival, but these inherited differences do not.
stem.evolab.island_detective_question: Who has the better survival chance here?
stem.evolab.island_detective_changed_res: Conditions changed before survival. These are the chances in the recorded habitat; your original prediction is not scored.
stem.evolab.island_detective_no_predicti: This round ran before you locked a prediction. You can still investigate the evidence.
stem.evolab.island_detective_match: Your prediction matches the model’s chances. That does not tell us which individual must survive.
stem.evolab.island_detective_rethink: The model’s chances suggest a different answer. Compare the factors below: no single trait tells the whole story.
stem.evolab.island_detective_surprise: Chance surprise: the resident with lower odds survived.
stem.evolab.island_detective_chance_less: Each resident gets its own random survival draw. Both, one, or neither may survive. Survival also does not guarantee offspring.
stem.evolab.island_detective_formula_hel: The simulation multiplies temperature, predator, energy and food factors, then limits the result to 2–95%. Factors below are rounded; they are teaching choices, not measurements from real animals.
stem.evolab.island_detective_neutral_for: With trait selection off, every resident has the same chance: 0.68 × the habitat’s food factor.
stem.evolab.island_detective_costs: Insulation matters relative to the cold. Coat match and legs affect predator protection. Long legs use energy; insulation adds a cost in warm habitats.
stem.evolab.island_detective_hold: This advances your island once, holding this habitat for that round. Your Living climate setting continues afterward.
stem.evolab.island_detective_stale: The habitat or selection setting changed. Start a new case to predict under the current conditions, or restore the original settings.
stem.evolab.island_detective_pair_note: These residents were chosen for contrast, not as a random population sample. A new case replaces this card. Saving updates the detective journal entry.
stem.evolab.island_quest_cold_question: Who leaves offspring when winter arrives?
stem.evolab.island_quest_family_question: How far will one spriglet’s family reach?
stem.evolab.island_quest_drift_question: Can traits change without an advantage?
stem.evolab.island_quest_intro: Choose a guided investigation or explore freely. Each uses your current population and holds the climate steady. Your island history stays with you.
stem.evolab.island_quest_unavailable_end: Start a new expedition below for another full investigation. Your existing evidence remains available to review and export.
stem.evolab.island_quest_unavailable_pas: Return to the present to start an investigation. You can still explore this recorded generation.
stem.evolab.island_quest_changed: Settings changed during this investigation. You can still record it as exploratory evidence.
stem.evolab.island_quest_extinct: The population ended early. Extinction is an observation: review the final survivors and record what happened.
stem.evolab.island_quest_ready: Your evidence is ready. Replay the result generation, then collect a field note. An unexpected result counts as a discovery too.
stem.evolab.island_quest_active: Follow the island through the next generations. Playback pauses when your investigation reaches its result.
stem.evolab.island_replay_wait: Advance once to reveal which parents survived and what their offspring inherited. You can replay the same evidence as often as you like.
stem.evolab.island_replay_parent_hint: These are the parents before survival was sampled. Their genes stay the same throughout their lives.
stem.evolab.island_replay_survivor_hint: These are the actual survivors, still in their original places. Everyone else left no offspring in this round.
stem.evolab.island_replay_child_hint: These are new individuals. Each inherited one allele per trait from each of two surviving parents.
stem.evolab.island_replay_dots: Each dot is one organism; the dark line marks the mean.
stem.evolab.island_replay_selection: Traits and chance both affected survival. The offspring mean can shift again through inheritance and random sampling.
stem.evolab.island_replay_neutral: Trait advantages were off. Differences here arise from random survival, inheritance, and any mutations—not a survival advantage for a trait.
stem.evolab.island_variation_intro: Choose a range to find its organisms on the island. Bar height shows the share of this cohort on a fixed 0–100% scale.
stem.evolab.island_variation_bounds: Ranges include the lower value and stop before the upper value; the last range includes 100. Unrounded trait values determine the groups.
stem.evolab.island_variation_empty: No organisms fall in this range in the current stage. Try another stage or range.
stem.evolab.island_variation_find: Find this range on the island
stem.evolab.island_variation_compare: How common was this range at each stage? Compare proportions as well as counts.
stem.evolab.island_variation_cohorts: Compare this range across the recorded round
stem.evolab.island_variation_start: Advance once to compare this range among recorded parents, survivors and offspring.
stem.evolab.island_variation_not_family: A trait range is not a family. Matching offspring are new individuals; a change in one round does not establish its cause. An empty cohort has no percentage.
stem.evolab.island_survival_scale: Colored fill = modeled survival probability. Tap a bar to inspect. Genes and coats stay unchanged.
stem.evolab.island_survival_recorded_sub: These organisms actually survived this recorded round. Their bars show their original probabilities, not 100% certainty. Survivors are a selected subset of the parents.
stem.evolab.island_survival_recorded_par: These are the probabilities the parents faced in this recorded round. Open the table to compare them with actual survival outcomes.
stem.evolab.island_survival_hypothetical: For these residents, this is a what-if estimate in the displayed habitat, not a recorded survival result. A later round may use different conditions.
stem.evolab.island_survival_next_change: Living climate will change the habitat before the next survival draw
stem.evolab.island_survival_still_displa: The bars still describe the habitat displayed now.
stem.evolab.island_survival_neutral_help: Trait advantages are off. Every resident has the same chance here: 0.68 × the habitat’s food factor. Random survival still occurs.
stem.evolab.island_survival_equal: Every organism has the same modeled chance in this view.
stem.evolab.island_survival_table_captio: Modeled probabilities in the displayed habitat; values are rounded.
stem.evolab.island_survival_empty: There are no organisms in this view, so no individual survival probabilities to display. Revisit the parents or survivors.
stem.evolab.island_survival_limit: A higher chance is not a promise of survival or offspring. These probabilities come from this teaching model; they are not measurements from real animals.
stem.evolab.island_lenses_subtitle: See the variation hiding in plain sight.
stem.evolab.island_lenses_hint: Choose an inherited trait or survival chance to reveal bars above the spriglets. Inspect contrasting residents, then follow a recorded generation.
stem.evolab.island_lens_scale: Colored fill = trait value (0–100). Tap a bar to inspect. Coats and genes stay unchanged.
stem.evolab.island_lens_equal: All have the same value for this trait.
stem.evolab.island_lens_extremes: One example at each extreme; ties are possible.
stem.evolab.island_lens_empty: No organisms in this view. Choose another replay stage or generation to inspect their traits.
stem.evolab.island_lens_not_fitness: Higher is not always better. A trait’s effect depends on the habitat, and survival still includes chance.
stem.evolab.island_highlights_intro: Find a moment worth investigating, revisit the actual island, and keep it in your collection. These are observations from your expedition, not proof of a general pattern.
stem.evolab.island_highlights_empty: Advance a generation to record survival, inheritance and new variation. Highlights appear only when something has actually been recorded.
stem.evolab.island_highlight_habitat_que: The new habitat was in place before this survival round. Which inherited differences might matter here? Compare the parents with the actual survivors.
stem.evolab.island_highlight_shift_quest: These are parent and offspring cohort means on a 0–100 scale. Did the shift appear during survival, or between survivors and offspring? Replay all three cohorts to investigate.
stem.evolab.island_highlight_extinction_: Fewer than two parents survived, so the model produced no offspring. Extinction is evidence too: revisit the survival round without changing its outcome.
stem.evolab.island_highlight_survival_qu: Who survived is only part of the story. Which survivors actually left offspring, and how much variation reached the next generation?
stem.evolab.island_highlight_mutation_qu: A mutation is new variation, not an automatic upgrade. Meet this offspring and trace its inherited copies; older records may not contain the exact mutation draws.
stem.evolab.island_highlight_selection_o: Traits affected survival in this recorded round; chance still mattered.
Survival was trait-neutral in this recorded round.
stem.evolab.island_highlight_visit: Revisit this moment on the island
stem.evolab.island_highlight_full: Your six spaces are full. Select a kept moment and remove it to make room.
stem.evolab.island_highlight_picker_help: Suggestions select the latest habitat change, lowest survival share, largest absolute one-generation mean shift, a birth with the most recorded mutations, and extinction when present. Ties use the earliest generation. This deliberately selective view does not replace the complete data or establish causes. Kept moments remain available as the expedition continues.
stem.evolab.island_highlight_save_help: Saving updates the collection’s own journal entry. Your written field note and other investigations stay separate.
stem.evolab.island_report_kicker: A closer look at what happened
stem.evolab.island_report_no_offspring: There is no offspring cohort, so no new trait mean to compare. Revisit the actual survivors to investigate why the population ended.
stem.evolab.island_report_selection: A mean can shift through survival differences, inheritance and chance. One generation alone does not establish adaptation.
stem.evolab.island_report_neutral: Trait advantages were off in this round. Any mean shift comes from chance survival and inheritance, with mutation only when recorded.
stem.evolab.island_report_total_mutation: new allele mutations in this cohort
stem.evolab.island_story_parents_help: These are the recorded parents before survival was sampled. Each arrived with its own inherited combination; none can change its genes to meet a new need.
stem.evolab.island_story_survivors_help: These individuals survived this round. Their positions and genes are unchanged. Traits affected their chances, but favorable traits never guaranteed survival.
stem.evolab.island_story_survivors_neutr: These individuals survived this round by trait-neutral sampling. Any difference in the trait mean here came from chance, not a survival advantage.
stem.evolab.island_story_offspring_help: A new cohort inherits one allele from each of two surviving parents at every locus. The parents have not transformed into these offspring. Random mutation can add new variants.
stem.evolab.island_story_offspring_empty: Fewer than two individuals survived to breed. There is no offspring cohort or mean trait to report. The recorded parents and survivors remain available to investigate.
stem.evolab.island_forecast_kicker: Your call, before the round runs
stem.evolab.island_forecast_traits: Traits influence the odds; chance is part of each outcome.
stem.evolab.island_forecast_neutral: Trait advantages are off. Equal chances do not guarantee equal outcomes.
stem.evolab.island_forecast_invalid: Choose a whole number from 0 to the population size.
stem.evolab.island_forecast_average: Adding every resident’s survival probability gives an expected survivor count of
stem.evolab.island_forecast_average_help: That is an average over many repetitions with these same residents and conditions, not a promise for this round. The actual count must be a whole number.
stem.evolab.island_forecast_once: Locking runs one real generation with the coming habitat. Exploring the clue does not run the simulation.
stem.evolab.island_draw_intro: The simulation gives each individual a uniform random number from 0 up to, but not including, 1. It survives when that number is strictly below its survival probability.
stem.evolab.island_draw_above: At or above: does not survive
stem.evolab.island_draw_trial_evidence: This explains the selected trial. The recorded round keeps its own outcome.
stem.evolab.island_draw_practice_help: Drag the blue marker or use the slider below. The spriglet’s probability stays fixed; only this practice number changes.
stem.evolab.island_draw_practice_fails: This practice draw does not pass
stem.evolab.island_draw_equal: Exactly at the threshold: the strict less-than rule means it does not survive.
stem.evolab.island_draw_practice_below: The practice number is below the survival threshold.
stem.evolab.island_draw_practice_above: The practice number is above the survival threshold.
stem.evolab.island_draw_practice_boundar: Practice values include the endpoints. Actual random draws stay below 1. Practice changes do not sample a trial or change the island.
stem.evolab.island_draw_fresh: Every individual gets its own draw. A new trial uses fresh draws with the same original traits and probabilities.
stem.evolab.island_chance_resident_intro: Choose a spriglet, then switch trials to follow its outcomes. Its inherited traits and modeled chance stay the same.
stem.evolab.island_chance_resident_group: Survivors in the recorded round and selected trial
stem.evolab.island_chance_resident_same_: Same survivor count, different individuals. Matching totals can hide different outcomes.
The same individuals survived in this comparison. Another trial can still differ.
stem.evolab.island_chance_resident_chang: {changed} of {total} individuals have different outcomes in the recorded round and this trial.
stem.evolab.island_chance_resident_proba: Modeled survival chance in every trial
stem.evolab.island_chance_resident_scale: Inherited traits · 0–100 teaching scale. Higher is not always better.
stem.evolab.island_draw_open: Chance microscope: see the survival draw
stem.evolab.island_chance_resident_frequ: Survived {count} of {total} explored trials. This observed share can differ from its modeled probability.
stem.evolab.island_chance_resident_bound: Trial survival does not change the recorded life or imply offspring. Each trial gives the original individual a fresh survival draw.
stem.evolab.island_chance_kicker: Same parents. Same habitat. Fresh survival draws.
stem.evolab.island_chance_intro: Try another possible survival outcome. Every trial starts with all the same parents and their original chances, including parents that did not survive your recorded round.
stem.evolab.island_chance_empty: Your recorded round stays fixed. Add trials to discover the range of possible counts.
stem.evolab.island_chance_progress: {trials} of 20 trials explored. Latest trial: {latest} survivors. Counts so far: {low}–{high}.
stem.evolab.island_chance_chart_help: Each bar is one trial; height shows its survivor count. The darker bar is the trial you are inspecting.
stem.evolab.island_chance_lesson: Same traits and conditions can give different outcomes. A small set of trials need not average to the expected count; it does not tell us which outcome must happen next.
stem.evolab.island_chance_boundary: These trials repeat survival only. No offspring are produced, and your island history stays unchanged.
stem.evolab.island_forecast_locked_help: your forecast. Reveal the survivors to compare with the recorded result.
stem.evolab.island_forecast_match: Your forecast matched this round. A match does not make the next outcome certain.
stem.evolab.island_forecast_difference: The recorded count differed from your forecast. Each organism faced its own random draw, so even a well-reasoned estimate can differ from the result.
stem.evolab.island_forecast_result_help: An expected count is a long-run average, not a target the simulation tries to reach. Surviving also does not guarantee offspring.
stem.evolab.island_watch_once: This round is recorded. Exploring its stages does not run it again.
stem.evolab.island_story_control_hint: Replay only: the expedition does not advance. Pause to inspect, or choose a stage above.
stem.evolab.island_inherit_parents_help: Each parent has two alleles for this trait. An allele is a version of a gene.
stem.evolab.island_inherit_choose_help: The highlighted copies were randomly selected when this offspring was born. Each parent contributes one.
stem.evolab.island_inherit_variation_hel: A recorded mutation may change a copied allele. Changes happen without knowing what the habitat will favor.
stem.evolab.island_inherit_result_help: In this model, the offspring’s trait is the average of its two inherited values. Its genes now stay fixed for its lifetime.
stem.evolab.island_inherit_title: How this offspring inherited its traits
stem.evolab.island_inherit_legacy: This saved birth has no detailed copy record. You can compare the parent and offspring values below; the exact choices and mutation events are unknown. New generations record every choice.
stem.evolab.island_inherit_scale: Values use a 0–100 teaching scale and are rounded. Higher is not always better.
stem.evolab.island_siblings_help: Compare other offspring from this birth generation. Exploring these recorded relatives keeps your selected spriglet and the island unchanged.
stem.evolab.island_siblings_full_help: Full siblings share both recorded parents, even when the parents appear in a different order.
stem.evolab.island_siblings_half_help: Half siblings share exactly one recorded parent. Their other parents differ.
stem.evolab.island_siblings_no_full: No other offspring with both of these parents was recorded in this birth generation.
stem.evolab.island_siblings_no_half: No other offspring sharing exactly one of these parents was recorded in this birth generation.
stem.evolab.island_resemblance_scale: 0–100 teaching scale; values are rounded. Higher is not always better.
stem.evolab.island_siblings_variation: Sharing parents does not guarantee identical traits. Allele copies are sampled at each birth; mutations can also contribute. Matching trait values do not prove identical genes.
stem.evolab.island_resemblance_below: This offspring’s trait value is lower than both parents’ values.
stem.evolab.island_resemblance_above: This offspring’s trait value is higher than both parents’ values.
stem.evolab.island_resemblance_within: This offspring’s trait value falls within the parents’ range.
stem.evolab.island_resemblance_mechanism: In this model, the offspring averages its two inherited allele values. It does not simply average the parents’ trait values.
stem.evolab.island_resemblance_pair_help: Choose one copy from each parent. These possibilities use the parents’ actual alleles before any mutation; exploring them does not create an organism.
stem.evolab.island_resemblance_equal: First copy label: Parent 1. Second: Parent 2. Each pairing has a 1 in 4 chance in this model. Different pairings can produce the same trait value.
stem.evolab.island_resemblance_unknown: This older birth has no detailed copy record. The possible pairings are known; which one occurred and whether mutations happened are unknown.
stem.evolab.island_resemblance_no_mutati: Neither inherited copy mutated for this trait. Different combinations alone can make offspring differ from both parents.
stem.evolab.island_resemblance_mutated: of the two inherited copies mutated for this trait. Mutation is random with respect to what the habitat favors.
stem.evolab.island_life_inherited: Two parents; a new combination of inherited alleles.
stem.evolab.island_life_founder: One of the founding residents. No earlier parents are recorded.
stem.evolab.island_birth_compare_help: Meet the two parents behind this spriglet’s inherited traits. You can explore this birth even before its own survival round.
stem.evolab.island_life_changed: The habitat changed after this organism was born. Its inherited traits stayed the same.
stem.evolab.island_life_cohort_survived: residents survived this round. Chance is part of every result; one outcome does not tell us which trait caused it.
stem.evolab.island_life_limit: This expedition ends at generation 60. A later survival outcome is unknown.
stem.evolab.island_life_pending: This round has not happened yet. Use Watch a generation to discover what happens.
stem.evolab.island_life_children_help: Each offspring is a new individual with alleles from two parents. Choose any one to continue the story.
stem.evolab.island_family_no_offspring: This organism survived but left no recorded offspring. Survival does not guarantee parenthood.
stem.evolab.island_life_no_children: It did not survive to reproduce, so it left no direct offspring in this round.
stem.evolab.island_life_no_partner: Fewer than two residents survived. This model needs two distinct surviving parents to produce offspring.
stem.evolab.island_resemblance_title: Compare this offspring with both parents
stem.evolab.island_life_children_pending: No result yet. Unrecorded offspring are unknown, not zero.
stem.evolab.island_life_model: In this model each generation replaces the last. Surviving parents do not remain as residents. Revisit a stage without changing the recorded result.
stem.evolab.island_family_showing: Showing the first four. Explore the next generation for the rest.
stem.evolab.island_family_pending: This organism’s next generation has not been recorded yet.
stem.evolab.island_family_not_survived: This organism did not survive the next round. Its traits remain unchanged in the record.
stem.evolab.island_family_trace_help: Choose a parent or offspring to visit its birth generation. Follow the same family as its traits are reshuffled.
stem.evolab.island_inheritance_trace_hel: The first allele comes from the first parent; the second comes from the second parent. A new value indicates a mutation during inheritance. Displayed values are rounded. Matching values do not identify which identical copy was inherited.
stem.evolab.island_nickname_help: A field label, not an inherited trait. Leave blank to use the original field name.
stem.evolab.island_pressure_scale: Relative teaching scale: 0–100. These are model settings, not field measurements.
stem.evolab.island_pressure_neutral: Trait-neutral survival: food still affects the chance of survival, but coat, insulation and legs do not.
stem.evolab.island_next_climate: Living climate changes the habitat before survival.
stem.evolab.island_repeat_help: Start each pair again with the exact same organisms, habitats and mutation rate. Change the random survival and inheritance events, then follow five rounds or extinction.
stem.evolab.island_repeat_main_safe: Your main island and original pair stay unchanged.
stem.evolab.island_repeat_missing: pairs have an extinction; their trait difference is undefined.
stem.evolab.island_repeat_chart_alt: B minus A for each paired trial. Left means A is higher; right means B is higher. Exact values and extinctions are in the table.
stem.evolab.island_repeat_tolerance: Differences within 0.1 point count as similar. A higher value is not necessarily an advantage. This is a descriptive comparison, not a test of statistical significance.
stem.evolab.island_repeat_table: Read every trial and random seed
stem.evolab.island_repeat_table_help: Means use a 0–100 scale. Extinct populations have no trait mean; each endpoint lists its actual generation.
stem.evolab.island_repeat_interpret: Look for a direction that repeats, and for exceptions. These trials test chance with one starting population. Try different founding populations and conditions before extending the conclusion.
stem.evolab.island_repeat_invite: Would fresh random events tell the same story? Record a repeat to find out.
stem.evolab.island_trial_table_caption: Latest recorded populations. Trait means use a 0–100 teaching scale; no mean exists after extinction.
stem.evolab.island_trial_chart_alt: Mean insulation in A and B over five rounds. Solid green is A; dashed ochre is B. Recorded values are in the comparison table.
stem.evolab.island_trial_chart_key: Mean insulation · A: solid green · B: dashed ochre. Lines end at the last living population.
stem.evolab.island_trial_limits: Both copies start with the same genes and random stream. Different survivor and offspring counts can make later random events diverge. A single paired trial combines selection and chance; repeat with fresh seeds before making a general claim.
stem.evolab.island_trial_fixed: Both climates stay fixed. Mutation chance per inherited allele:
stem.evolab.island_trial_main_waits: Your main expedition waits here, unchanged: generation
stem.evolab.island_trial_question: What if the same population faced a different future?
stem.evolab.island_trial_setup_help: Copy your present population into A and B. Change one condition in B, then follow both for five rounds. All other starting settings match. The main island does not advance.
stem.evolab.island_trial_toggle_off: In B, survival ignores traits. Random survival, inheritance, mutation and drift still occur.
stem.evolab.island_trial_toggle_on: In B, inherited traits affect survival. In A, survival remains trait-neutral.
stem.evolab.island_trial_shared_creature: spriglets with identical genes in both copies.
stem.evolab.island_trial_fixed_setup: Both climates will be held steady. Names, family tracking and field notes stay with your main island.
stem.evolab.island_trial_extinct_help: This branch has no later generations. Its partner can continue.
stem.evolab.island_compass_help: Choose a question. Your island holds the evidence.

stem.evolab.island_model_title: How this world works · teacher notes
stem.evolab.island_model_body: Spriglets are fictional organisms in a simplified population-genetics model. Three independent diploid loci control continuous traits; one allele per locus comes from each of two randomly sampled surviving parents. The trait is the average of its two alleles. Survival depends on habitat, coat camouflage, insulation, leg length, food, and chance. Longer legs aid escape but cost energy. Mutations happen during inheritance, with no knowledge of the environment.
stem.evolab.island_model_limits: Generations do not overlap. At least two survivors are needed to breed. The next population has 2.65 offspring per survivor, rounded down and capped at 60. Carrying capacity, trait effects, and mutation rates are teaching choices, not measurements. The model omits migration, linkage, dominance, learned behavior, age structure, and reproductive isolation. It does not simulate the full evolutionary process or demonstrate speciation.
stem.evolab.island_teacher_prompt: Try a 10-minute investigation: inspect two founders; predict the effect of a long winter; hold that habitat for five generations; compare allele pairs in parents and offspring. Repeat with a fresh seed. Then disable trait-based survival to investigate drift. A single run cannot separate all causes of change.
stem.evolab.island_landscape_model_note: The scenery draws inspiration from Galápagos lava shores, arid scrub, and greener highlands. This is a fictional island, not a geographic replica. Winter is an experimental climate, not a Galápagos season. Terrain, plants, water, and scenic viewpoints are visual context: all spriglets experience the selected habitat, regardless of position. This tool follows inherited traits across generations; the Ecosystem tool explores interactions between species and resources.
